title: Father turns to private investigator after son's death
subtitle: Desperate for answers after his son's death, Rulia Owaan hired a lawyer and a private investigator to probe the incident.
article: Desperate for answers after his son's death, Rulia Owaan hired a lawyer and a private investigator to probe the incident.

Peel officers had been executing a search warrant at a Caledon residence on Jan. 16, 2006, when Rajesh Owaan was shot and killed. The search warrant was part of an investigation into the kidnapping of a Brampton truck driver.
Owaan, who fired twice at police, was shot at nine times after he refused to drop his weapon, officials in the Special Investigations Unit said. The SIU's investigation cleared police.

"We weren't told what happened by the SIU or the police. Nobody told us anything," Rulia Owaan said, speaking in Hindi during an interview at his home in Concord, Ont. "We only read it the next day in the paper."

Rulia wanted to meet with the SIU, but the first time his lawyer set up a meeting, he was too grief-stricken to go. Instead, he went to India, hoping the change of scenery would help him get over his loss. When he returned, he met with the SIU, where he was read their official report that cleared the officers of any wrongdoing.
The investigators Owaan hired visited the scene on Jan. 27 and Jan. 30 to take photographs and measurements of the home where the standoff took place.

In total, they took 387 photographs. Images of shattered glass, scattered playing card, spattered blood and a toy truck lying in the snow were among them. But they concluded they didn't have enough information "to draw any conclusions or to formulate any theories based strictly on the scene evidence."

Owaan's lawyer sent him a copy of the news release issued by the SIU after it cleared the officers of wrongdoing. The lawyer included a letter that explained: "the SIU does not provide copies of its report to members of the public, including family of deceased persons."

The lawyer said that SIU director James Cornish and the investigator were willing to meet with Owaan. But at this point, the father declined the offer. His son was gone, and his own questions would remain unanswered.
